paper_role: architecture composition gate between ranked-I/O feasibility and full FLUX backbone integration
question: Can one scalar-only skip entry point compose the K=2 predictor, the exact non-stochastic FlowMatch Euler update, and aliased latent write-back for a complete A12/50-step cache schedule?

frozen_system.schedule: FLUX.1-dev 50-step dynamically shifted FlowMatch Euler sigmas
frozen_system.scheduler: latent.float() + (sigma_next - sigma) * noise.float(), rounded once to BF16

entry_points.cache_anchor_step: full actual noise plus delta sigma

gates.C1_numerical_composition: Every one of 50 latent states and the final latent must be bit-exact against the host predictor plus FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler algebra.
gates.C2_skip_boundary: Across all 38 skip calls, full-tensor host writes and reads must both be zero; only coefficients and delta sigma may enter.
gates.C3_state_lifecycle: Initialize resets anchors and latent for a request; finalize exposes exactly one full latent at the request boundary.

scope_limit: Actual anchor noise tensors are synthetic frozen BF16 inputs in this experiment. Anchor ingress still originates on the host; H1c-b must feed ranked output from the real FLUX backbone before any end-to-end speed claim.

decision.if_pass: Replace the synthetic anchor source with real ranked FLUX backbone output and run a full denoise-loop A/B.
decision.if_fail: Do not proceed to full backbone integration until predictor, scheduler, and latent state share an exact executable contract.
